exdoc.title: Forestry Revocation and National Parks Reservation Act 1984

attrib.name: title
attrib.value: Forestry Revocation and National Parks Reservation Act 1984

block.txt: An Act to revoke certain dedications of parts of State forests and part of a timber reserve and to reserve or dedicate the lands the subject of those revocations, and certain other Crown lands, as parts of national parks, a nature reserve and part of a nature reserve.
This Act may be cited as the Forestry Revocation and National Parks Reservation Act 1984.

heading.b: Revocation of parts of certain State forests

block.txt: The dedications as parts of State forests of the lands described in Schedule 1 are revoked.

heading.b: Revocation of part of a timber reserve

block.txt: The reservation as part of a timber reserve of the land described in Schedule 2 is revoked.

heading.b: Reservation of lands as parts of national parks

block.txt: The lands described in Part 1 of Schedule 1 are reserved as part of the Washpool National Park.
The lands described in Part 2 of Schedule 1 are reserved as part of the Dorrigo National Park.
The lands described in Part 3 of Schedule 1 and in Schedule 2 are reserved as parts of the Werrikimbe National Park.
The lands described in Part 4 of Schedule 1 and in Schedule 3 are reserved as parts of the Barrington Tops National Park.

heading.b: Dedication of lands as a nature reserve or as part of a nature reserve

block.txt: The lands described in Part 5 of Schedule 1 are dedicated as a nature reserve to be known as “Mount Hyland Nature Reserve”.
The lands described in Part 6 of Schedule 1 and in Schedule 4 are dedicated as parts of the Mount Seaview Nature Reserve.
Schedule 5 has effect.

heading.b: Reservation of lands as parts of national parks

block.txt: The lands reserved as parts of national parks by section 4 shall, for the purposes of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 (other than section 35 of that Act), be deemed to have been so reserved by proclamation made under section 33 (3) of that Act.

A reference in the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 (other than in section 35 of that Act), to the publication of a proclamation under section 33 (3) of that Act shall, in relation to a reservation referred to in section 4, be deemed to be a reference to the enactment of this Act.

heading.b: Dedication of lands as nature reserve

block.txt: The lands dedicated as a nature reserve by section 5 (1) shall, for the purposes of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 (other than section 35 of that Act as applied to nature reserves by section 58 (b) of that Act), be deemed to have been so dedicated by proclamation made under section 49 (1) of that Act.

The lands dedicated as parts of a nature reserve by section 5 (2) shall, for the purposes of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 (other than section 35 of that Act as applied to nature reserves by section 58 (b) of that Act), be deemed to have been so dedicated by proclamation made under section 49 (2) of that Act.

A reference in the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 (other than in section 35 of that Act), being a reference to, or a reference to be construed as a reference to, the publication of a proclamation under section 49 (1) or (2) of that Act shall, in relation to a dedication referred to in section 5, be deemed to be a reference to the enactment of this Act.

The name assigned to a nature reserve by section 5 (1) shall be deemed to have been assigned to that reserve by a proclamation referred to in section 51 (a) of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.

heading.b: Existing leases under the Forestry Act 1916

block.txt: Section 42 (2) of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, applies to and in respect of a lease under the Forestry Act 1916, being a lease:
affecting any of the lands described in Parts 1–4 of Schedule 1, and
current and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act,
in the same way as it applies to a licence or permit under the Forestry Act 1916, affecting lands within a national park.
Section 55 (2) of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, applies to and in respect of a lease under the Forestry Act 1916, being a lease:
affecting any of the lands described in Parts 5 and 6 of Schedule 1, and
current and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act,
in the same way as it applies to a licence or permit under the Forestry Act 1916, affecting lands within a nature reserve.
In this clause, existing interest means a lease, licence, permit or occupancy current and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act.

The administration of matters relating to existing interests, to the extent that those interests affect any of the lands described in Schedules 1–4, is vested in the Minister administering the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.
For the purposes of subclause (2), the Minister administering the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, shall have:
in respect of existing interests under the Forestry Act 1916—the powers of the Minister administering that Act, and
in respect of existing interests under the Crown Land Management Act 2016—the powers of the Minister administering that Act.
A revocation effected by this Act does not affect anything done or omitted to be done before the commencement of this Act.
Forestry Revocation and National Parks Reservation Act 1984 No 85. Assented to 27.6.1984. This Act has been amended as follows:
Crown Land Legislation Amendment Act 2017. Assented to 17.5.2017.
